wsl-claude, on 'does R19 still wait on R16?': that block is YOUR condition (transportPending.js:105-111: 'the database decision is blocked on this by Andy's own condition'), and it's a good one. But it doesn't need to stay a separate step. R16 asks 'what must each log row carry to PROVE what it claims' (today: peer, hash, payload, and no signature). R19 asks 'what table do the rows go in'. Those are the SAME question: the table's columns ARE R16's answer. Designed apart, we'd build the table, then migrate it again when R16 adds the signature and the sealed text.
So I'd not lift R16 but FOLD it in: the first item of this session is 'what each row stores, so it can prove sent, received and acted-on', and the table follows from it. One design, one migration.

Board rule built (57c04ae): ending design mode keeps the board, and your first Team line of a new design clears it. On 'attach warnings later, so we don't lose too much': I read it as don't hold the move for R16. Rows go into the table now with what they carry today, a row that can't prove itself gets a warning mark later, and nothing already logged is lost. If that's right, it cuts against wsl's 'one design, one migration': adding the proof columns later is a second migration. That's cheap in SQLite (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, old rows empty) but still real. Did I read you right, or did you mean a warning before the board clears?

One suggestion for the first item, the interfaces one. R19.1: 'The log moves behind its existing api: nothing above trafficLog.js changes, and the rows go into one new table in node.db.' Why first: it fixes the size of everything that follows. trafficLog.js:98-103 already promises that when reads hurt, a local database goes behind this same api block and nothing above will notice, because nothing above knows the filename (storeOwnership.js guards that). node.db already exists (nodeStore.js:108), so no new file and no new dependency. What's still to argue: a new table in node.db is a core persist shape, so it needs peer review and your yes. That makes this item 'core, needs your gate' in wsl's terms. Add it?
